title: Client Feedback Evidence Collector
description: Collects chats, voice notes, emails, and attachments into one local workflow for clear, traceable client feedback.
seoTitle: Client Feedback Evidence Collector Case Study
seoDescription: How a local command-line tool turns WhatsApp and Gmail feedback into traceable evidence packets with attachments and transcripts.
role: Product design and command-line tool implementation
constraints: Client feedback can include private message text, audio, and attachments, so the tool had to keep run outputs local by default.
WhatsApp evidence had to come from a linked browser session because the project does not use an official WhatsApp API.
Gmail collection had to preserve reusable files and records without exposing access tokens, browser storage, or live mailbox data.
problem: Useful client feedback was spread across WhatsApp chats, voice notes, and domain Gmail threads, which made it hard to assemble a reusable evidence packet without manual copying and fragile exports.
The workflow needed repeatable collection, local transcription, attachment capture, and organized run records without sending sensitive evidence to another service.
solution: Built a Rust command-line tool that checks local dependencies, searches and collects WhatsApp messages, and searches and collects Gmail threads with stable output for automation.
Used a dedicated browser profile for WhatsApp Web, extracted visible chat messages, downloaded visible voice notes, converted them to a standard audio format, and optionally transcribed them locally.

Added a separate Gmail collection path that resolves the selected messages or thread, downloads attachments locally, writes a readable evidence document, and records a unique fingerprint for each file.
result: Turned scattered client feedback sources into a repeatable local workflow that writes `run.json`, `messages.json`, `evidence.md`, attachments, audio files, WAV files, and transcript artifacts.
Kept the public code limited to collection rules and local file handling while leaving private evidence directories, authentication state, cookies, and browser storage out of the repo.

Backed the brittle parts with unit tests for WhatsApp metadata parsing, Agent Browser snapshot parsing, download normalization, Gmail attachment decoding, filename sanitization, and command-output JSON parsing.
